title: KV index rollover stresslog
content:
Purpose:
Quick scratchpad to capture commands, logs, small reproducer attempts and hypotheses for the KV-index rollover / sequence-length boundary failures seen in prod on model-rw-2b. Intend to keep this as an actionable checklist I can refer back to while pairing with SRE. NOT a postmortem.

Summary of failure mode observed: 
- Under long-chat sessions (avg user seqlen 12k tokens) we occasionally saw repeated token divergence + memory spikes and then requests returning 500 with kernel-select errors.
- Error surface: kernel selection picked an 'optimistic' fused-attn kernel and later failed when KV index pointers wrapped past expected window.
- Trigger looks correlated with dynamic batching + prefix caching enabled + occasional sequence resets mid-session (user edits) — i.e., non-monotonic sequence id progression.

Immediate reproduction attempts (local cluster, gpu-staging):
1) Baseline single-request repro (failed to reproduce reliably):
   # launch small server with model-rw-2b (quantized q4f16), enable prefix cache in config
   docker-compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml up --build -d serving-runtime

   # script to stream tokens and then issue a session edit (reset seq id to earlier value)
   python reproduce_kv_rollover.py --model model-rw-2b --tokens 12000 --edit-at 6000

   Observed: 90% of runs completed fine. ~10% returned mismatch between token outputs (diverged on token 6021) with logs below.

2) Stress loop (parallel 40 clients, high QPS)
   for i in `seq 1 40`; do python reproduce_kv_rollover.py --parallel-client $i & done
   Observed: after ~18 minutes memory spikes on GPU0 and many kernel-select fallback messages.

Key log snippets (from /var/log/serving/runtime.log):
[2025-02-17T14:22:09Z] WARN kernel_select: selected kernel fused_attn_opt_v2 for model-rw-2b seq_len=8192 batch=4
[2025-02-17T14:22:09Z] ERROR kv_cache: index_rollover_detected uid=session-09a3 ptr=0x7f8a1b4c offset=8388608 window=8388608
[2025-02-17T14:22:09Z] ERROR request_handler: request_id=rcv-5f33e kernel_select_failure: incompatible-kv-index, falling back=legacy_attn
[2025-02-17T14:22:09Z] ERROR request_handler: request_id=rcv-5f33e client=mobile-android code=500 msg="internal kernel failure"

Minimal stack trace (from stdout):
  at kv_cache::read_index (kvcache.cc:214)
  at rr::KVReader::get (kv_reader.cc:87)
  at attention::Compute::run (attn_compute.cc:451)
  at serving::Worker::handle_request (worker.cc:1023)

Commands & quick instrumentation hacks I ran locally:
- Add verbose index print just before selection: (kvcache.cc)
  fprintf(stderr, "KVIDX: uid=%s start=%u end=%u ptr=%p\n", uid, start_idx, end_idx, ptr);
- Force kernel selection logic to require stable monotonic seq id for fused kernels: set ENV DEBUG_FORCE_MONOTONIC=1 then restart.
- Temporary mitigation: disable fused_atten kernel by env: SERVING_DISABLE_KERNEL=fused_attn_opt_v2 — reduces error rate to <1% in stress run but greatly increases latency.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Non-monotonic session sequence ids (due to client-side edit/resend) corrupts KV index pointer arithmetic in continuous-batching path, causing pointer to equal window size (exact boundary), which triggers rollover detection logic only in optimized kernel paths.
2) Kernel selection assumes aligned KV index ranges (<window) and does not properly handle wrap-around when base pointer == window. Edge case leads to off-by-one in index computation.
3) Race between cache-eviction GC and a long-running attention compute where eviction marks page as recycled but compute still references old pointer (use-after-free-like symptom).
4) Quantization path interacts with index math (packed layout) exposing different pointer alignment that fused kernels depend on.

Small experiments to validate hypotheses: 
- For hypothesis 1: simulate non-monotonic seq id by sending updates where session.seq_id resets to a lower value mid-stream and assert kvcache returns contiguous entries (script is reproduce_kv_rollover.py).
- For hypothesis 2: add unit tests for kernel selection with synthetic KV indices exactly equal to window boundary and run kernel selector in isolation (kernel_select_test.cc). Expect to see off-by-one.
- For hypothesis 3: instrument GC to emit 'evict-id' for each page and add sequence number; run stress and look for overlapping timestamps between compute start and evict event.
- For hypothesis 4: run the same stress with the non-quantized float model build to compare failure rate.

Notes on one interesting repro run (2025-02-17 14:22:09):
- CPU log shows session.seq_history: [0..5999, 6010..12000] (gap + manual edit at 6000).
- KVIDX log: start=6010 end=14370 ptr=0x7f8a1b4c window=8388608 -> ptr arithmetic resulted in end-start == window (bad).
- Fused kernel chosen because batch size metrics indicated high throughput; fallback recommended by runtime and did occur but only after user-experienced 500.

Short-term mitigations we can push quickly: 
- Hotfix: in kernel selector, require an additional sanity check: if (end - start) >= window -> force fallback to legacy kernel and increment metric kvcache.kernel_sanity_fail.
- Disable prefix caching for sessions flagged as 'editable' until we have reliable monotonic seq guarantees from client. (Client-side flagging is feasible via header X-Session-Mode).
- Add alert on kvcache.index_rollover_detected with top-10 session ids and last 20 seq events.

Longer-term engineering items: 
- Rework kvcache pointer arithmetic to use saturating arithmetic and explicit sequence epoch tracking so monotonicity isn't required for correctness.
- Add end-to-end test harness for non-monotonic seq_id patterns (CI job).
- Consider making fused_attn_opt_v2 robust to wrap-around by checking and normalizing indices before kernel invocation; coordinate with kernel authors (PR linked above).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we accept small latency hit on heavy sessions to guarantee correctness (i.e., conservative kernel selection)? Tradeoff analysis needed.
- Determine whether any customer data was affected (audit logs + request ids). Ticket INF-1127 assigned to CS to contact impacted tenants.
- Validate whether the issue reproduces on different GPU architectures (A100 vs H100). My initial runs were on A100; schedule H100 runs tomorrow.

Quick action checklist for next pairing session: 
- [ ] Roll hotfix requiring sanity check in kernel selector (small PR, test locally).
- [ ] Add ephemeral metric emission for index_rollover_detected (to prod).
- [ ] Run non-quantized stress runs on H100.
- [ ] Coordinate with Marisol for client header rollout to flag editable sessions.

Logs & snippets appended to the ticket. Will keep this doc updated with experiment IDs and final remediation plan once we confirm root cause.

Signature:
Ayesha Patel (eng-serving-runtime)
Notes: leaving raw command history below for reproducibility.

Raw commands run during debugging session: 
# start staging cluster
./scripts/staging-up.sh --image serving-runtime:canary-2025-02-17
# run single repro
python reproduce_kv_rollover.py --model model-rw-2b --tokens 12000 --edit-at 6000 --log-kvidx
# run parallel stress
./scripts/run-parallel.sh reproduce_kv_rollover.py 40 --args "--tokens 12000 --edit-at 6000"
# kernel select unit test
bazel test //runtime/kernel:kernel_select_test --test_output=errors
# metrics tail (local)
kubectl logs -n canary serving-runtime-0 -c runtime --tail=500 | rg "index_rollover_detected"
